title: Electric light control experiment (15 subjects, 4 classes, 31 EEG ch)
description: EEG recordings from 15 healthy participants performing a visual P300 oddball paradigm for controlling an electric light as a home appliance via a brain-computer interface. Data were acquired with 31 active EEG channels at 500 Hz while participants attended to flashing stimuli on an LCD display in a 4-class setup. Each participant completed 50 training and 30 online testing blocks. The dataset supports development and benchmarking of ERP-based BCIs and inter-subject transfer learning.
methods_description: 31-channel EEG was recorded with an actiCHamp (Brain Products) amplifier at 500 Hz, using active electrodes in the standard 10-20 layout and a linked-mastoid reference. Visual flash stimuli were presented on an LCD display with a 750 ms stimulus onset asynchrony. Each participant completed one session with 50 training and 30 online testing blocks.
